newsitem.title: POLAND: Former Yeltsin adviser fears show trial in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Former Yeltsin adviser fears show trial in Russia.

text.p: A former adviser to Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Sunday he feared he would become the victim of a political show trial if he returned to Russia.

"The accusation against me has to do not with corruption but with political intrigues," Sergei Stankevich said in an interview with Polish public teleivision following his release from a Warsaw jail on Friday.

"Should I return to take part in a show trial, be subjected to the inhuman conditions of a Russian jail or perhaps become the victim of intrigues, provocations and violence without even the benefit of a trial?" he asked.
But he said he would not oppose returning to Moscow to clear his name if he had assurances of a truly impartial hearing.
Stankevich, who had grown a beard as a disguise, was detained in Poland on April 19 on the basis of an international warrant for his arrest.
He is accused of accepting a bribe in 1992 to allow a concert to take place in Moscow's Red Square, a charge he denies.
"In Russia's history there has been a sad tradition of staging show trials, not only in the 1930s, but even quite recently," Stankevich said.
"When the (Russian) authorities want to show people how active they are, they resort to such methods.
"Two weeks before my arrest (in Poland), a crackdown on corruption was announced in Moscow. Somebody apparently wanted to show results after only two weeks."

The television said Stankevich was interviewed at his Polish solicitor's Warsaw office and "spoke very slowly, carefully choosing his words." It added: "He preferred not to speak about his conflict with Yeltsin and Russian special services."
Asked about his plans, Stankevich said he would not request political asylum but hoped to apply for permanent-residence status in Poland.
He planned to write two books, including one on Stalin's 1940 Katyn massacre of Polish officers and officials, and later hoped to work as a consultant.
